new_statements.quote: Stress is usually not indicated, since it regularly falls on the penultimate syllable in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages. Only the exceptions to this rule are marked. [...] Most exceptions to the general stress rule are well-motivated (either a phonetically long vowel is shortened (cf. §3.4.6 above) or stress moves to the first member of a sequence of unlike vowels as in táipang 'mango', which occurs as an alternate to the regular taípang). | [p.10, Indonesian:] Secara teratur penekanan dalam bahasa-bahasa Tomini Tolitoli muncul pada suku kata kedua dari akhir, contohnya: Dampelas polu 'batu' diucapkan [pólu] dan bukan [polú], betuong 'bintang' [betúoŋ] dan bukan [bétuoŋ], dsb.
new_statements.translation: Indonesian part: 'Regularly, stress in the Tomini-Tolitoli languages falls on the second syllable from the end, for example: Dampelas polu "stone" is pronounced [pólu] and not [polú], betuong "star" [betúoŋ] and not [bétuoŋ], etc.' The same page continues: 'often in a VVKV sequence it is the first and not the second vowel that receives stress, as for instance in Dampelas kangkáula "spider" not kangkaúla, ndóupo "not yet" not ndoúpo'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word, counted after suffixation (possessive suffixes shift stress rightwards so it stays penultimate; clitics and free forms do not). The Dampelas echo paragogic vowel (bunta'A, tasi'I etc.) is treated as superficial and does not move the stress. Exceptions: in a sequence of unlike vowels (non-high + high, e.g. kangkáula, ndóupo, táipang) stress may fall on the first vowel of the sequence, i.e. on the antepenult; shortened phonetically long vowels.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress is defined only as the lengthening of accented reduplicated syllables (marked with a grave accent), with speaker variation in how strongly the reduplicated syllable is stressed (sec. 3.5.10, p.81).
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate stress in words with a non-high + high vowel sequence (VVKV), e.g. Dampelas kangkáula 'spider', ndóupo 'not yet', group-level táipang 'mango' (variable); shortened long vowels; Balaesang-only stress on final short closed syllables (not Dampelas); Lauje-only final stress after final-vowel deletion (not Dampelas). Himmelmann 1991 (NUSA 33 p.51) adds that stress 'remains penultimate when suffixes or clitics are added'; 'exceptions to this rule are very few in number'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is made for 'all Tomini-Tolitoli languages' as a group, with Dampelas cited as the example language in the Indonesian version; domain is the phonological word (stem + suffixes), based on elicited citation-form word lists (ca. 1200 items per language; Dampelas data first-hand, collected 1988-1993 in Talaga/Sioyong/Sabang). The source is a sourcebook/wordlist compilation with a phonological introduction, not a full grammar.
new_statements.identity_note: Source covers the whole Tomini-Tolitoli group; Dampelas (damp1237, incl. the nearly extinct Dampal dialect of Ogoamas/Bangkir, sec. 2.2.1.3 p.25) is in Himmelmann's first-hand sample (word lists DAM from Talaga, Sioyong and Sabang, 1988-1993) and is the example language in the Indonesian stress paragraph (p.10). Stress rule is stated group-level ('all Tomini-Tolitoli languages'), not in a Dampelas-only section.

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 Stress, printed p.51 (PDF p.3, verified on page image): 'Stress placement is very regular in Tomini-Tolitoli languages and thus empirically defines the domain of (word) phonology. It falls on the penultimate syllable of a (phonological) word and remains penultimate when suffixes or clitics are added' (ex. Lauje ba'i / ba'inye); exceptions very few: Lauje paragogic vowel (stress stays on antepenult), ultima stress after final-vowel deletion in Lauje (sec. 2.4), antepenultimate in <10 of ca. 1200 items with non-high+high vowel sequences (sec. 2.5), a Totoli sub-rule.
